messages.subject: dsm.var.gam estimating CVs as NA  !! :(
parts:
Hi Listfolk!

I'm running a DSM (with soapfilm smoother) on line transect data for humpback whales in southeast Alaska. I think I have decent working model (though I have not yet gone fully through rigorous model selection), but when I attempt to calculate coefficients of variation and a CI, dsm.var.gam only produces NAs :(

Part of what confuses me is that, if I split my prediction grid for plotting, I do get a plot with CVs, but I can not get a total CV.  

Any ideas how to fix this, what I might be doing wrong??

The objects used below are too large to attach here but I'm happy to share them via personal email!!
#-the dsm object: SoapA1_depth   ## a Soap film spatial smooth with depth as a covariate
#- the prediction grid: km3Predgrid  ## a 3x3km grid (I have also tried this w/ 1x1km and 2x2km with the same results)
#- dsm.var.gam output objects:  soapA1_depth_Var3km , soapA1_depth_Var3km_p ## summary output below


>  km3PredgridNA.RM <- km3Predgrid[!is.na(km3Predgrid$DEPTH),]

> ## running dsm.var.gam to get total CV
> soapA1_depth_Var3km <- dsm.var.gam(SoapA1_depth,km3PredgridNA.RM, off.set = km3PredgridNA.RM$off.set)

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] dsm.var.gam estimating CVs as NA !! :(
parts:
Hi Abigail, hi listfolk,

I think the issue here is that there is an NA in one of the covariates
or one of the prediction grid cells is outside of the soap boundary.

Your solution of using:

km3PredgridNA.RM <- km3Predgrid[!is.na(km3Predgrid$DEPTH),]

is along the right lines.

What you can do is look at the output of the split version of the
estimate and use that to locate the problem cells. So:

then look at the $pred element (giving the predicted values). You can
obtain the indices of the "bad" cells using which():

bad_inds <- which(is.na(soapA1_depth_Var3km_p$pred))

Then you can look into what is wrong with those cells:

km3Predgrid[bad_inds, ]

if none of the predictors are NA, then it's possible that their
locations are outside of the soap boundary (or too close to it), in
which case you should be able to see this by plotting.

If that doesn't work then please drop me an e-mail and we can look into it.


hth
--dave
